What stays on your phone, and the one thing that doesn\'t

Focus Pocus has no server and no account. Your blocklists, pacts, rituals, history and streaks live in this app\'s private storage and are never uploaded. Automatic cloud backup is switched off for this app, so they are not quietly copied to Google either.

The apps you guard and the rules you set. Focus session history, block events, and your streaks. Per-app open counts, including the reflex opens shown on the pact screen, kept for 30 days. Mana, boons, trials and sigils. Your settings.
It leaves the phone only when you export it yourself, to a file you choose.
The one thing that can leave

Crash reports, if you allow them. A report carries the stack trace, your device model, and the Android and app versions — never your blocklists, the names of apps you guard, your usage, or anything from your screen.
The Share Analytics switch on the previous screen turns this off, and it takes effect at once.

No account, name, email or contacts. No location. No advertising ID — the permission is stripped out of the app at build time. No ads and no cross-app tracking, ever: ads in a focus app would refute the whole point.

One thing: the package name of the app that just came to the foreground. It subscribes to window-change events only and never asks Android for window content, so it cannot read your screen, your typing, or your passwords. Notification access, when you grant it, is used only to dismiss notifications from blocked apps — their contents are never read or stored.

Take your data with you from Settings → Backup → Export. Turn off crash reports with Share Analytics. Delete everything by uninstalling, or from Android\'s Settings → Apps → Focus Pocus → Storage → Clear data.
Questions, or to have crash reports deleted: cdwilliams40@gmail.com

Focus Pocus uses Android\'s AccessibilityService API for exactly one thing: noticing which app comes to the foreground, so the apps you chose to guard can be blocked or redirected. It listens only to window-change events — it cannot read screen content, keystrokes, or passwords. Nothing it observes leaves your device or is shared with anyone.
Save your enchantments, pacts, rituals, history, and settings to a file — a reinstall or a new phone shouldn\'t cost you your streaks. Live session state and running seals stay on the device.
